name: Real
tsum_exp_neg_mul_int_sq
result.type:
∀ {a : ℝ},
  0 < a → ∑' (n : ℤ), Real.exp (-Real.pi * a * ↑n ^ 2) = 1 / a ^ (1 / 2) * ∑' (n : ℤ), Real.exp (-Real.pi / a * ↑n ^ 2)
result.value:
:= by
  simpa only [← ofReal_inj, ofReal_tsum, ofReal_exp, ofReal_mul, ofReal_neg, ofReal_pow, ofReal_intCast, ofReal_div,
    ofReal_one, ofReal_cpow ha.le, ofReal_ofNat, mul_zero, zero_mul, add_zero] using
    Complex.tsum_exp_neg_quadratic (by rwa [ofReal_re] : 0 < (a : ℂ).re) 0
result.informal_name: Poisson Summation Formula for Gaussian Functions
result.informal_description: For any positive real number $ a $, the infinite sum over all integers $ n $ of $ \exp(-\pi a n^2) $ equals $ \frac{1}{\sqrt{a}} $ times the infinite sum over all integers $ n $ of $ \exp\left(-\frac{\pi n^2}{a}\right) $. Formally, $ \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} \exp(-\pi a n^2) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{a}} \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} \exp\left(-\frac{\pi n^2}{a}\right) $.

name: Finset
abs_sum_le_sum_abs
result.signature:
{G : Type*} [AddCommGroup G] [LinearOrder G] [IsOrderedAddMonoid G] (f : ι → G) (s : Finset ι) :
  |∑ i ∈ s, f i| ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, |f i|
result.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {G : Type u_9} [inst : AddCommGroup G] [inst_1 : LinearOrder G] [IsOrderedAddMonoid G] (f : ι → G)
  (s : Finset ι), |∑ i ∈ s, f i| ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, |f i|
result.informal_name: Triangle Inequality for Finite Sums: $|\sum_{i \in s} f(i)| \leq \sum_{i \in s} |f(i)|$
result.informal_description: For any additive commutative group $G$ equipped with a linear order and compatible addition (i.e., an ordered additive commutative monoid), any function $f : \iota \to G$, and any finite set $s \subseteq \iota$, the absolute value of the sum of $f(i)$ over $s$ is less than or equal to the sum of the absolute values of $f(i)$ over $s$. This generalizes the classical triangle inequality to finite sums in ordered algebraic structures.

name: HurwitzKernelBounds
isBigO_atTop_F_int_one
result.signature: (a : UnitAddCircle) : ∃ p, 0 < p ∧ F_int 1 a =O[atTop] fun t ↦ exp (-p * t)
result.type: ∀ (a : UnitAddCircle), ∃ p, 0 < p ∧ HurwitzKernelBounds.F_int 1 a =O[Filter.atTop] fun t => Real.exp (-p * t)
result.value:
:= by
  obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := a.eq_coe_Ico
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hp'⟩ := isBigO_atTop_F_nat_one ha.1
  obtain ⟨q, hq, hq'⟩ := isBigO_atTop_F_nat_one (sub_nonneg.mpr ha.2.le)
  refine ⟨_, lt_min hp hq, ?_⟩
  have : F_int 1 a =ᶠ[atTop] fun t ↦ F_nat 1 a t + F_nat 1 (1 - a) t :=
    by
    filter_upwards [eventually_gt_atTop 0] with t ht
    exact F_int_eq_of_mem_Icc 1 (Ico_subset_Icc_self ha) ht
  refine this.isBigO.trans ((hp'.trans ?_).add (hq'.trans ?_)) <;> apply isBigO_exp_neg_mul_of_le
  exac...
result.informal_name: Exponential Decay Bound for Hurwitz Kernel at Infinity
result.informal_description: There exists a positive real number $ p $ such that the Hurwitz kernel periodic sum function $ F_{\text{int}}(1, a) $ is asymptotically bounded by $ O(e^{-p t}) $ as $ t \to \infty $, uniformly for all $ a \in \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z} $.

name: SummationFilter
instLeAtTopSymmetricIcc
result.type:
∀ {G : Type u_2} [inst : AddCommGroup G] [inst_1 : PartialOrder G] [IsOrderedAddMonoid G]
  [inst_3 : LocallyFiniteOrder G], (SummationFilter.symmetricIcc G).LeAtTop
result.informal_name: Symmetric Interval Summation Filter is Less Than or Equal to At Top Filter
result.informal_description: The summation filter generated by symmetric closed intervals $[-g, g]$ as $g$ increases is less than or equal to the at_top filter in the filter order.

name: AddValuation
map_le_sum
result.signature: {ι : Type*} {s : Finset ι} {f : ι → R} {g : Γ₀} (hf : ∀ i ∈ s, g ≤ v (f i)) : g ≤ v (∑ i ∈ s, f i)
result.type:
∀ {R : Type u_3} {Γ₀ : Type u_4} [inst : Ring R] [inst_1 : LinearOrderedAddCommMonoidWithTop Γ₀] (v : AddValuation R Γ₀)
  {ι : Type u_6} {s : Finset ι} {f : ι → R} {g : Γ₀}, (∀ i ∈ s, g ≤ v (f i)) → g ≤ v (∑ i ∈ s, f i)
result.informal_name: Additive Valuation Inequality for Finite Sums
result.informal_description: Let $ v $ be an additive valuation from a ring $ R $ to a linearly ordered additive commutative monoid with top element $ \Gamma_0 $. For any finite set $ s $ of indices, function $ f : s \to R $, and element $ g \in \Gamma_0 $, if $ g \leq v(f(i)) $ for all $ i \in s $, then $ g \leq v\left(\sum_{i \in s} f(i)\right) $. This establishes that the valuation of a finite sum is bounded below by the common lower bound of the valuations of its terms.

name: Real
sin_pos_of_mem_Ioo
result.signature: {x : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ Ioo 0 π) : 0 < sin x
result.type: ∀ {x : ℝ}, x ∈ Set.Ioo 0 Real.pi → 0 < Real.sin x
result.informal_description: For any real number $x$ in the open interval $(0, \pi)$, it holds that $\sin x > 0$.

name: Real
abs_sin_eq_sin_abs_of_abs_le_pi
result.value:
:= by
  rcases lt_or_ge x 0 with h | h
  · rw [abs_of_neg h, sin_neg, abs_of_nonpos (sin_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_neg_pi_le h.le (abs_le.1 hx).1)]
  · rw [abs_of_nonneg h, abs_of_nonneg (sin_nonneg_of_nonneg_of_le_pi h (abs_le.1 hx).2)]
result.informal_description: For any real number $x$ satisfying $|x| \leq \pi$, the absolute value of $\sin x$ is equal to $\sin |x|$, i.e., $|\sin x| = \sin |x|$.

name: Real
mul_abs_le_abs_sin
result.value:
:= by
  wlog hx₀ : 0 ≤ x
  case inr => simpa using this (by rwa [abs_neg]) <| neg_nonneg.2 <| le_of_not_ge hx₀
  rw [abs_of_nonneg hx₀] at hx ⊢
  exact (mul_le_sin hx₀ hx).trans (le_abs_self _)
result.informal_name: Lower Bound for Absolute Sine on $[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}]$
result.informal_description: For any real number $x$ satisfying $|x| \leq \frac{\pi}{2}$, it holds that $\frac{2}{\pi} |x| \leq |\sin x|$.

name: Real
sinc
result.value:
:=
  if x = 0 then 1 else sin x / x
result.informal_description: The function maps a real number $ x $ to $ 1 $ if $ x = 0 $, and to $ \frac{\sin x}{x} $ otherwise.

name: Real
sin_nonneg_of_mem_Icc
result.signature: {x : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ Icc 0 π) : 0 ≤ sin x
result.type: ∀ {x : ℝ}, x ∈ Set.Icc 0 Real.pi → 0 ≤ Real.sin x
result.value:
:= by
  rw [← closure_Ioo pi_ne_zero.symm] at hx
  exact closure_lt_subset_le continuous_const continuous_sin (closure_mono (fun y => sin_pos_of_mem_Ioo) hx)
result.informal_description: For any real number $ x $ in the closed interval $[0, \pi]$, the sine of $ x $ is non-negative, i.e., $ \sin(x) \geq 0 $.
